extraction.name: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language, formulated as multiple-choice question answering over goal-solution pairs.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to glance at the instructions, then construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and a valid solution; they also provided a permutation/trick that sounded reasonable but was wrong. Additional qualification and validation HITs were run, and low-agreement examples were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: How-to instructions from instructables.com were used as the source/scaffold for annotation prompts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples; train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples were validated and low-agreement examples removed; data was truncated at 150 tokens for experiments, affecting about 1% of the data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to produce a physical goal, a valid solution, and a trick/incorrect solution based on instructable-inspired prompts. Qualification HITs were used before the main HIT, and validation HITs were run afterwards. Annotators had to achieve over 80% on qualification to participate, and human evaluation used annotators who achieved at least 90% on the qualification HIT.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed. Human performance was calculated by majority vote.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 solutions per item (one correct solution and one trick/incorrect solution)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: AFLite; BERT-Large embeddings were used within AFLite; the transformers library was used for model experiments.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as a benchmark for advancing language understanding of physical commonsense, with potential relevance to robots and language models that interact with the world.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note reporting bias in physical commonsense text and state that they used AFLite to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples. They also aimed to flatten the distribution of referenced objects because annotators tended to prefer prototypical kitchen or garage tools.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by reporting bias, and some correct examples requiring expert-level domain knowledge were removed during validation because they were considered outside commonsense. The paper also notes that some development errors were actually correct but required web search to verify.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking physical commonsense understanding; training, development/validation, and testing splits are provided. The paper also evaluates models on the dataset for testing and analysis.
